sentences.text:
This Writ Petition (Civil) Having Come Up For Admission On
16.11.2023, The Court On The Same Day Delivered The Following:
 Wp(C) No. 37913 Of 2023 : 2 :
Abdul Khader vs The Project Director on 16 November, 2023

Aggrieved by Ext.P1 award passed by the 3rd respondent determining the compensation in respect of a property acquired from the petitioner comprised in re- survey No.162/9 (R.S.No.162/2A old) of Thekkil Village, Kasaragod Taluk, he has filed Ext.P2 arbitration application before the 2nd respondent/ Arbitrator, invoking the provisions under Section 3G(5) of the National Highways Act,
1956 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short).
Ext.P4 is the award passed by the 3 rd respondent, in respect of another property acquired from the petitioner comprised in re-survey No.246/7 (246/1C old) of the same Village.
Challenging Ext.P4 award also, the petitioner has preferred Ext.P5 arbitration application before the 2nd respondent under Section 3G(5) of the Act.

The grievance of the petitioner is that, though the applications were filed as early as on 19.02.2023,
so far they are not disposed of.
The petitioner states that he is a senior citizen and the delay in disposal of the arbitration applications is causing undue hardships to him.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Standing Counsel appearing for the NHAI and the learned Government Pleader.
3.

In the facts and circumstances of the case and having considered the submissions made across the Bar, there will be a direction to the 2 nd respondent to consider and dispose of Exts.P2 and P5 arbitration applications, as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within a period of eight months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment, after hearing the petitioner and the NHAI.
The writ petition is disposed of as above.

Sd/-
